result.notes: 128 bits with 0 errors has no discriminating power: expected errors at theoretical Pb=0.00239 is only 0.31 (P(0 err)=0.74), and the exact one-sided 95% upper confidence bound for 0/128 is 0.02313, about 9.7x the theoretical Pb; even a true Pb=1% (~4.2x theory) would give 0 errors with probability 0.28. Hence the measurement cannot certify BER matches theory; ~41871 bits would be needed for ~100 expected errors. Claim not supported.
